_v1_notes.PERPETRATOR|MECHANISM: each mechanism requires a specific authority. Only the contracting officer controls the specification and can split purchases. Only suppliers can rig bids among themselves. Only someone with payment authority can inflate invoices or take a kickback on release, which is the senior official; the intermediary participates in kickbacks and can broker bid rigging but holds no authority alone.
_v1_notes.PERPETRATOR|DETECTION ROUTE: bank monitoring catches only those handling cash - the senior official and the intermediary. A losing bidder complaint catches conduct visible in the tender, so it misses the senior official and the intermediary who act after award or outside the process. Internal audit is blind to supplier-side collusion and to an external intermediary.
_v1_notes.PERPETRATOR|CONTRACT VALUE: below threshold there is no tender, so no bidding supplier, no senior sponsorship and no intermediary role - only the contracting officer raising small orders.
_v1_notes.MECHANISM|DETECTION ROUTE: bid rigging leaves no buyer-side trail so internal audit is N. Invoice inflation and split purchases produce no losing bidder to complain. Kickbacks leave nothing in procurement records and no losing bidder. Bank monitoring sees only the kickback.
_v1_notes.MECHANISM|CONTRACT VALUE: specification manipulation and bid rigging both require a competitive tender, so both are N below threshold. Split purchases are the definition of threshold avoidance and are N at mid and major value where the aggregate is visible.
_v1_notes.DETECTION ROUTE|CONTRACT VALUE: a losing bidder complaint is N below threshold because there are no losing bidders.
